title: Cast Iron vs. PVC in Drainage Systems
description: Selecting the right piping material for Drain-Waste-Vent (DWV) systems depends heavily on acoustic performance, fire resistance, and structural requirements. Schedule 40 PVC is lightweight, chemical-resistant, and cost-effective, making it a standard choice for residential DWV applications. However, cast iron pipe excels in multi-story residential and commercial buildings where sound attenuation is critical. Heavy cast iron pipe walls absorb the sound of rushing wastewater, preventing drainage noise from echoing through wall cavities into living spaces. Additionally, cast iron offers superior fire-resistance ratings at structural wall penetrations. Understanding material characteristics ensures the ideal balance of performance, occupant comfort, and code compliance.
caption:
Cast Iron vs. PVC in Drainage Systems

Selecting the right piping material for Drain-Waste-Vent (DWV) systems depends heavily on acoustic performance, fire resistance, and structural requirements. Schedule 40 PVC is lightweight, chemical-resistant, and cost-effective, making it a standard choice for residential DWV applications. However, cast iron pipe excels in multi-story residential and commercial buildings where sound attenuation is critical. Heavy cast iron pipe walls absorb the sound of rushing wastewater, preventing drainage noise from echoing through wall cavities into living spaces. Additionally, cast iron offers superior fire-resistance ratings at structural wall penetrations. Understanding material characteristics ensures the ideal balance of performance, occupant comfort, and code compliance.
